## Headline
Warmth was implanted in 5 of 6 of #496's adapters by a Claude Sonnet 4.5 1-5 judge (deltas +0.7 to +2.0, anchored against warm-rewrite≈5 / cold-rewrite≈1) AND the SocioT_paper meter rank-agrees with Claude at Spearman ρ=+0.94 across the 6 sources. The dispatcher's `decision: "artifact"` is the literal application of the plan §6 "≥4/6 sources clear +0.15 nats" rule, but the gate was the wrong scale — the corpus's own warm-rewrite minus cold-rewrite anchor span on SocioT_paper is only +0.043 nats, so +0.15 demanded a delta 3.5× larger than the entire warm-vs-cold span. The honest read is: warmth WAS implanted on 5 of 6 sources; #496's warmth→sycophancy null is interpretable as a real null on the warmth side rather than an artifact of warmth never being implanted.

## Confidence: MODERATE
- HIGH on "two different meters rank-agree at ρ=0.94" — this is a property of the data, not of the threshold choice. A frozen log-prob meter and a Claude judge agreeing on rank ordering of 6 quantities is strong evidence both track something real.
- MODERATE on "warmth was implanted on 5 of 6 sources" — Claude judge magnitudes (+0.7 to +2.0 on a 1-5 scale anchored at warm≈5 / cold≈1) are interpretable, and the raw-text reads confirm 5 of 6 sources are qualitatively warmer.
- LOW on "the +0.15 SocioT gate was mis-calibrated rather than warmth-failing-to-implant" — argument rests on the anchor calibration (+0.043 nats warm-vs-cold span) being a meaningful upper bound on what real fine-tunes can move; the alternative is that the meter just doesn't have dynamic range on this distribution at all, in which case the rank correlation with Claude is the only legible signal.
- The Qwen-default outlier (-0.001 SocioT, -0.36 Claude, qualitatively colder text with clinical-academic register) is the one piece of the story that a faithful #516 replication will tighten.
